chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Bashir from Ibn Abi Ghufaylah, al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, from Bashir ibn Abi Ghaylan al-Shaybani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrifices of the Jews, the Christians, and the Nasibis ( those of the Sunnis). He turned his cheek and said: 'All of them are until a day that is not.'

key_terms.إِلَى يَوْمٍ مَا: Until a day that is not

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of Jews, Christians, and Nasibis according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the permissibility of consuming the meat of Jews, Christians, and the *Nasibis* (those opposed to the Ahl al-Bayt). His gesture of turning his cheek (*fayala bi-shadqihi*) signifies a nuanced dismissal, while the phrase 'until a day that is not' (*ila yawmin ma*) is interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating indefinite validity until the Day of Judgment, affirming the general permissibility of *Ahl al-Kitab* meat while potentially distinguishing the status of the *Nasibis*. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the covenant of the People of the Book remains valid for dietary purposes unless specific conditions of impurity or enmity are proven otherwise.
